comments.author: mrob
comments.story_title: Tutorial series for simulating NES Graphics (2018)
comments.why_zh: 举例说明用 Raspberry Pi 卡带向 NES 的 PPU 送数据
comments.quote_zh: Tom Murphy 用 Raspberry Pi 实现了这个
comments.text_zh: 注意，其中一些特性需要卡带里特殊的硬件支持。NES 卡带连接器引出了 CPU 和 PPU（图像处理单元）的引脚，最简单的游戏（“NROM”）就是把 ROM 芯片直接接到这些引脚上。更高级的设计会额外加一个内存管理控制器（通常称为“mapper”）：[LINK] 动态背景是靠 mapper 对字符（图块）内存做 bank switching 实现的。视差滚动则是靠 mapper 数扫描线，在到达正确的扫描线时产生中断，这样 CPU 就能在帧中途以正确的时机修改 PPU 的滚动寄存器。后来的 mapper，比如 MMC5，能精确控制帧中途的 bank 切换时机，从而支持屏幕上同时出现超过 256 个图块，并支持 8x8 而非 16x16 的属性块。终极的 mapper 会向 PPU 送入任意数据，模拟出带 8x1 属性块的位图显示（PPU 每 8 个像素才读一次属性内存，这是硬性限制）。Tom Murphy 用 Raspberry Pi 实现了这个（它并不完全适合这项任务，所以存在时序瑕疵，导致画面出现故障，但理论上可以做到没有这些瑕疵）：[VIDEO]
comments.text: Note that some of these features require special hardware support in the cartridge. The NES cartridge connector exposes CPU and PPU (picture processing unit) pins, and the simplest games ("NROM") connect ROM chips directly to them. More advanced designs add an additional memory management controller (commonly called a "mapper"): [LINK] The animated backgrounds are accomplished by the mapper bank switching the character (tile) memory. The parallax scrolling is accomplished by the mapper counting scanlines and generating an interrupt when the correct scanline is reached, so the CPU can change the PPU scroll registers mid-frame with the correct timing. Later mappers like the the MMC5 could precisely time mid-frame bank changes to support more than 256 tiles on screen at once, and to support 8x8 attribute blocks instead of 16x16. The ultimate mapper feeds arbitrary data to the PPU to simulate having a bitmapped display with 8x1 attribute blocks (the PPU only reads attribute memory once every 8 pixels, so that's a hard limit). Tom Murphy implemented this with a Raspberry Pi (which isn't ideally suited to the task, so there are timing imperfections causing graphical glitches, but theoretically it could be done without them): [VIDEO]

comments.author: silverlyra
comments.text_zh: 把 Prettier 当作一个软件工具来看，认为它比（比如）TypeScript 或 V8 更“基础”，确实像是一种层级倒置 [1]——但从历史、从实践的角度看，Prettier 让自动代码格式化（类似 `go fmt` 或 Python `black`）在 JavaScript 这门编程通用语中普及开来，这一成就是基础性的。过去那些盯着本可以更可读的代码、编写风格指南以及重新格式化代码所花的时间，现在都用来做我们最初想做的事了。而现在，通过用 Rust™ 重写它，来缩短我们等待应用格式化或在 CI 中检查格式的时间，又能帮我们多拿回一点时间。:) [1]: [VIDEO]
comments.text: When seeing Prettier as a software tool, to consider Prettier more “foundational” than (e.g.) TypeScript or V8 does seem like an inversion of hierarchy [1] – but viewed as history, as a practice, Prettier’s accomplishment of making automatic code formatting (à la `go fmt` or Python `black`) widespread in JavaScript, the lingua franca of programming, is foundational. All that time spent staring at code that could have been more readable, or writing style guides and reformatting code, is now spent doing what we were trying to do in the first place. And now, speeding up the time we wait to apply formatting or check it in CI by rewriting it in Rust™ gives us a bit more of that time back. :) [1]: [VIDEO]

comments.author: derefr
comments.text_zh: 你可以把旧式 x86 扩展硬件插到这块板上，并让它找到另一端一个 bug-for-bug 兼容的 x86 系统来通信。一个主要用例是嵌入式系统——例如工业控制系统。这类系统使用 1. 定制硬件——通常以扩展卡的形式——被造出来说 ISA 这类旧的、仅限 x86 的总线协议；以及 2. 旧的定制软件，设计为在 x86 CPU 上运行（通常是在 DOS 中），并通过那条总线直接与那套硬件通信。你不能随便给旧硬件的总线找个 USB 适配器，因为软件不会接受它。你也不能直接替换旧软件，因为新软件（无论是旧软件的新版本，还是其他厂商的软件）无法控制旧卡；而那块卡说的是该工业系统特有的、更低层（很可能是模拟信号！）的协议。通常，在这些旧系统上，定制扩展卡因为采用固态结构仍然能工作（谢天谢地；那张卡的厂商很可能早就没了！），但那张卡过去 40 年所栖身的旧 x86 机器正死于各种老电脑的毛病——或者就是无法被塞进受控工业系统新一代所强加的新外形规格里。在这种情况下，理想情况下你想找一个新的嵌入式宿主系统，由能用接下来 40 年的新部件构成，但仍然能以非常特定、定制、低层的方式与你的
comments.text: That you can plug legacy x86 extension hardware into the board, and have it find a bug-for-bug-compatible x86 system to talk to on the other end. A major use-case being embedded systems — e.g. industrial control systems. These systems use a combination of 1. custom hardware — usually in the form of peripheral cards — built to speak old legacy x86-only bus protocols like ISA; and 2. old custom software, designed to run on an x86 CPU (usually in DOS), and to speak directly to that hardware over that bus. You can't just find some USB adapter for the old hardware's bus, because the software won't take it. And you can't just replace the old software, because the new software (whether a newer version of the old software, or software from another vendor) won't control the old card; and the card speaks an even lower -level (probably analogue!) protocol specific to the industrial system. Often, on these old systems, the custom peripheral card is still working due to it being solid-state (and thank god for that; the card's vendor is probably long-gone!) but the old x86 box the card lived in for the last 40 years is dying of various old-computer maladies — or just can't be made to fit into a new form-factor forced by a newer generation of the industrial system being controlled.
